title: The year of mourning
translation: Nothing is sadder than a year of court mourning. The emperor moves into a mourning room: the floor is lowered, the blinds are made of reeds, the trim is rough cloth, and the furniture is plain. Everyone's clothes, swords and sword belts look different too. It's strange and solemn to see.
original: {諒闇|りやうあん}の{年|とし}ばかり{哀|あは}れなる{事|こと}はあらじ。
{倚廬|いろ}の{御所|ごしよ}のさまなど、{板敷|いたじき}をさげ、{葦|あし}の{御簾|みす}をかけて、{布|ぬの}の{帽額|もかう}あらあらしく、{御調度|おんてうど}ども{疎|おろそ}かに、みな{人|ひと}の{装束|さうぞく}、{太刀|たち}、{平緒|ひらを}まで、{異様|ことやう}なるぞゆゆしき。
literal: There is surely nothing as moving as a year of imperial mourning.

The look of the mourning hut residence and so on: lowering the board floor, hanging blinds of reeds, the cloth valances rough, the furnishings plain, and everyone's costume, swords, even sword sashes, being unusual: that is awesome.

notes.text: {諒闇|りやうあん}: the year of mourning the emperor observed for a parent. The whole court changed its dress and its rooms.
{倚廬|いろ}: a plain room the emperor moved into for the first days of mourning. The floor was set lower than usual, a sign of grief and humility.
ゆゆし: 'awe-inspiring, ominous, almost frightening'. ぞ … き: the attributive ending closes the ぞ. Kenkō lists the details of the change, and the strangeness of the familiar court is the point.
